newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu flat vs dlr, market awaits fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu flat vs dlr, market awaits fresh lows.

text.p: Romania's leu currency ended Thursday unchanged at 6,850/900 after inching down in the morning with traders bracing for weaker prices on the back of higher hard currency demand and inflationary expectations.
"Pressure on the leu is building up as the market is struggling to find a rate to lure dollar sellers. It will touch 6,950/7,000 early on Friday," said one trader.
Leu-dollar retail prices were at about 7,250/800 after plunging some 7.0 percent in early trading, but few currency shops were ready to sell dollars.
"The leu's retail prices should correct higher in the next few days, with money changing bureaux facing leu shortages," said one trader.

All traders said they were anxious to get details of a reform package, which the government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is expected to announce next Monday after loan talks with international lenders.

The government, seeking up to $1.0 billion in total loans from the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, have been working for more than one month on the reforms, including faster restructuring and privatisation of industry, as well as price and currency market liberalisation.
The Fund and the World Bank withheld credits to Romania last year over foreign exchange market curbs and overspending by the former ruling leftists in an election year.
Short-term money market rates hovered near 93 percent with traders expecting the average one-week refinancing rate to touch 100 percent against last week's 90 percent.
"With some players rushing to grab leu funds at Thursday's auction, prices might drift higher again," said one trader.
The central bank offered 600 billion lei in one-week funds on Thursday, unchanged from last week, when the one-week auctioned credit rate jumped to 90 from 81 percent.
